text: In Genesis 22 a question is raised and left unanswered. Abraham is commanded to take his son, his only son, whom he loves; and of what he feels we are told nothing, for the narrator never describes what passes within him. He makes no protest and offers no bargain. Abraham appears less as a character than as a silence, and that silence is the centre of the chapter; nothing in it recalls the man who argued for Sodom.
